study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Di Biase et al., Molecular Psychiatry, 2022
study_identification_part.si4_title: Cell type-specific manifestations of cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia

cm1_research_objectives.reason: Objectives are clearly stated: to test whether cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia relates to interregional variation in neural cell types using gene expression and genomics, and to use normative modeling to define deviation scores and patient subtypes validated with genetics. The purpose of applying normative modeling is explicit: establish normative ranges and quantify individual deviations to study heterogeneity and clinical/genetic links.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here, we sought to determine whether cortical thickness (CTh) heterogeneity in schizophrenia relates to interregional variation in distinct neural cell types... To characterize CTh heterogeneity, normative ranges were established for 34 cortical regions and the extent of deviation from these ranges was measured for each individual with schizophrenia... Regional alignment between CTh alterations with cell type transcriptional maps distinguished broad patient subtypes, which were validated against genomic data.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: For existing open datasets, the original publications for inclusion/exclusion criteria are cited. Image quality control and data completeness procedures are described, and final sample sizes are reported. Reasons for exclusion are partially provided (e.g., exclusion of HCP-1200 subjects with QC issues), but full eligibility criteria for healthy controls are not detailed within this paper.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Inclusion and exclusion criteria for each respective dataset are described elsewhere (HCP-Young adult [15]; HCP-Psychosis [16] and ASRB [17]). ... For the HCP-1200 cohort, subjects with documented brain anatomical, processing or noise issues (n=151) based on the HCP supplied 'QC_Issue' variable were excluded... (Discovery) n=1267 comprising 140 cases and 1127 controls; (Validation) n=520 comprising 335 cases and 185 controls.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly modeled in the normative quantile regression, and multi-site effects are addressed using ComBat harmonization while retaining age, sex, and diagnosis effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Quantile regression was used to obtain a normative range of regional CTh variation as a function of age and sex... Harmonization. Regional CTh estimates were retrospectively harmonized with ComBat to alleviate possible site-related differences, while retaining biological variation related to diagnosis, sex and age.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The sources of healthy control data are specified: HCP-Young Adult Sample and HCP-Psychosis for discovery, and ASRB for validation, with citations to originals.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: This study comprised a total of 1849 participants drawn from three independent datasets: (1) the Human Connectome Project-Young Adult Sample; (2) the Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis (HCP-psychosis); and (3) the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (ASRB).

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The study uses secondary/existing datasets for reference cohort data (HCP, ASRB). Per guidance, image acquisition protocol is not applicable for secondary data.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: The HCP-Young Adult Sample and HCP-psychosis datasets were acquired using very similar MRI protocols (see Supplementary Material), enabling them to be combined to form a single discovery cohort... The ASRB dataset was used to evaluate replicability and validity.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software (FreeSurfer v5.3 and v6) and steps are described, including intensity normalization, skull stripping, segmentation, surface reconstruction, atlas-based regionalization, and QC procedures following ENIGMA protocols.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: T1-weighted images comprising the ASRB dataset were processed using FreeSurfer version 6. Processing and CTh estimation for the HCP-psychosis dataset followed the HCP1200 pipeline... processed using FreeSurfer version 5.3. For all three datasets, preprocessing included intensity normalization, nonbrain tissue removal and spatial normalization... segmented into gray matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid... CTh was estimated... averaged over ... Desikan-Killiany atlas. Quality control... FreeSurfer quality control was performed as per ENIGMA protocols... All images satisfied reconstruction criteria...

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is defined as quantile regression with covariates (age, sex, interactions, quadratic age) and bootstrapped percentile CIs. Key model terms are described. Implementation software/library is not specified.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: Quantile regression was used to obtain a normative range... based on the following model... sex encodes the participant's sex... age is the participant's age... β2 is the rate at which CTh changes per year... β3 and β4 model the sex-by-age interaction and quadratic age effects, respectively. Bootstrapping was used to estimate confidence intervals for the 5% and 95% percentiles of regional CTh variation.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Coverage of the normative percentiles is assessed by reporting the percentage of individuals (controls and patients) outside the normative range across regions, which evaluates calibration of the model's prediction intervals.

Clinical implications are discussed via associations with cell-type PRS and patient subtyping. Directional semantics are only partially explained.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: Individuals with schizophrenia were positioned on the normative percentile charts and then a continuous measure of deviation (Δ) from the established normative range was expressed as a z-score...
